[p. 232]

This surah is Madani. Al-Kalbi said: except for His words, ﴿There is no private conversation of three but that He is their fourth﴾. And from ʿAta': the first ten verses of it are Madani and the rest are Meccan.

The majority of reciters read ﴿قَدْ سَمِعَ﴾ (qad sami'a) with clear pronunciation (bayan, i.e., without assimilation of the dal into the sin). Abu ʿAmr, Hamza, al-Kisa'i and Ibn Muhaysin read it with idgham (assimilation of the dal into the following sin). Khalaf ibn Hisham al-Bazzar said: I heard al-Kisa'i say: "Whoever reads qad sami'a and makes the dal clear before the sin, his tongue is foreign (a'jami), not Arabic." This statement is not to be considered; the majority hold to clear pronunciation.

The woman who pleads (al-lati tujadiluka) is Khawla bint Tha'laba — it is also said in diminutive form — or Khawla bint Khuwaylid, or Khawla bint Hakim, or Khawla bint Dulayj, or Jamila, or Khawla bint al-Samit. These are the views of the early scholars (al-salaf). Most narrators hold that the husband in this incident was Aws ibn al-Samit, brother of ʿUbada. It was also said that Salama ibn Sakhr al-Bayadi made zihar against his wife. His wife said: "O Messenger of Allah, Aws consumed my youth and I bore him children, and when I grew old and my family died, he made zihar against me." He said to her: "I do not see you except that you have become unlawful to him." She said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not do so, for I am alone and have no family other than him." He returned her to the same statement, and she returned to him. This is her pleading. During that, she was saying: "O Allah, I have young children from him. If I join them to him, they are lost; and if I join them to myself, they go hungry." This is her complaint to Allah, and the revelation came down during her pleading.

ʿAisha, may Allah be pleased with her, said: "Glory be to Him whose hearing encompasses all voices. Some of Khawla's speech was hidden from me, but Allah heard her pleading. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) sent for Aws and presented to him the expiation of zihar, freeing a slave. He said: 'I do not own [one].' Then fasting. He said: 'I am not able.' Then feeding. He said: 'I find nothing except that you help me.' So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) helped him with fifteen sa' [of dates], and prayed for him, and he made expiation by feeding and refrained from his wife." ʿUmar, may Allah be pleased with him, used to honour Khawla when she entered upon him and would say: "Allah has indeed heard her." Al-Zamakhshari said: The meaning of qad is expectation (tawaqquʿ), because the Prophet (ﷺ) and the woman were both expecting that Allah would hear her pleading and her complaint and send down what would relieve her. End of quotation.

Al-Harameyn and Abu ʿAmr read ﴿يَظَّهَّرُونَ﴾ (yazzahharun) with doubled letters (shadda); al-Akhawan and Ibn ʿAmir read ﴿يُظاهِرُونَ﴾ (yuzahiruna), the present tense of ẓāhara. Ubayy read ﴿يَتَظاهَرُونَ﴾ (yatazahharun), the present tense of tazāhara. And from him (Ubayy, or another narrator): ﴿يَتَظَهَّرُونَ﴾ (yatazahharun), the present tense of tazahhara. The meaning of all of them is zihar, which is a man's saying to his wife: "You are to me like the back of my mother," meaning in prohibition. It seems to be an allusion to riding, since their customary usage of the back refers to the backs of animals. The meaning is that he does not mount her as he does not mount his mother. For this reason the Arabs say, in contrast to this: "I dismounted from my wife," meaning: I divorced her. His words ﴿مِنكم﴾ (minkum, "of you") point to a rebuke of the Arabs and a censure of their custom of zihar, because it was among the oaths of the people of ignorance specifically, not of other nations.

The majority read ﴿أُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾ (ummahatihim) in the accusative (naṣb), according to the dialect of the Hijaz. Al-Mufaddal from ʿAsim read it in the nominative (raf'), according to the dialect of Tamim. Ibn Mas'ud read ﴿بِأُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾ (bi-ummahatihim) with an added bā'. Al-Zamakhshari said: "In the dialect of those who use the accusative." End of quotation. He means that the bā' is not added in the dialect of Tamim. This is not correct, and it has been refuted against al-Zamakhshari. The addition of bā' in phrases such as ﴿ما زَيْدٌ بِقائِمٍ﴾ (ma Zaydun bi-qa'im, "Zayd is not standing") is common in the dialect of Tamim. Al-Zamakhshari followed in this Abu ʿAli al-Farisi, may Allah have mercy on him.

Since the meaning of "like my mother's back" is "like my mother in prohibition," and the particular back that belongs to the body is not intended, the negation came with the words ﴿ما هُنَّ أُمَّهاتِهِمْ﴾ (mā hunna ummahātihim, "their wives are not their mothers"). Then He affirmed this with the words ﴿إنْ أُمَّهاتُهُمْ﴾ (in ummahatuhum, "their mothers are only"), i.e., in reality, ﴿إلّا اللّائِي ولَدْنَهُمْ﴾ (illa'l-la'i waladnahum, "except those who gave birth to them"). With them in prohibition He linked the mothers of foster-suckling (ummahat al-rida') and the mothers of the believers (ummahat al-mu'minin), the wives of the Messenger (ﷺ). Wives are not mothers in reality, nor are they joined to them. So the words of the one who makes zihar are "an objectionable word" (munkaran min al-qawl), which reality rejects and which the Sacred Law rejects. "And falsehood" (zuran) means a lie, baseless and deviating from the truth. It is forbidden with the prohibition of disliked acts in the extreme. When it occurs, it obligates (expiation). Allah, Exalted, gave hope after it with His words ﴿وإنَّ اللَّهَ لَعَفُوٌّ غَفُورٌ﴾ (wa inna Allaha la-ʿafuwwun ghafur, "And indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving"), together with the expiation. Al-Zamakhshari said: "﴿And indeed, Allah is Pardoning and Forgiving﴾ for what has passed from him if he repents of it and does not return to it." End of quotation. This is a Mu'tazili tendency.

The apparent view is that zihar occurs only with the mother alone. If he said, "You are to me like the back of my sister or my daughter," it would not be zihar. This is the view of Qatada, al-Sha'bi and Dawud, and a narration of Abu Thawr from al-Shafi'i. The majority — al-Hasan, al-Nakha'i, al-Zuhri, al-Awza'i, al-Thawri, Abu Hanifa, Malik, and al-Shafi'i in one view — said it is zihar. The apparent view is that the dhimmi (non-Muslim under protection) is not bound by his zihar, because of His words ﴿مِنكم﴾ ("of you"), i.e., of the believers. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i held this, because she is not among his wives. Malik said: he is bound by his zihar if he marries her, and it is valid from a revocably divorced wife (raj'iyya). Al-Muzani said it is not valid. Some scholars said: the zihar of one who has not consummated the marriage is not valid. If he made zihar against his slave-woman whom it is lawful for him to have intercourse with, it binds him according to Malik. Abu Hanifa and al-Shafi'i said it does not bind him. The cause of the disagreement is: does she fall under ﴿نِسائِهِمْ﴾ (nisa'ihim, "their wives") or not? The apparent view is that the zihar of a slave (ʿabd) is valid, because he falls under ﴿يُظاهِرُونَ مِنكم﴾ ("those of you who make zihar"), since he is one of the Muslims. If freeing a slave and feeding are impossible for him, he is able to fast. Al-Tha'labi related from Malik that his zihar is not valid, and that a woman is not included among "those who make zihar." So if she made zihar against her husband, it would be nothing. Al-Hasan ibn Ziyad said: she becomes one who has made zihar. Al-Awza'i, ʿAta', Ishaq and Abu Yusuf said: if she says to her husband, "You are to me like the back of so-and-so," it is an oath which she expiates. Al-Zuhri said: "I think she should make the expiation of zihar, and her saying this does not prevent her from being with her husband in intercourse."

The apparent meaning of God's words ﴿then they go back on what they said﴾ is that they return to the same wording that was said by them, namely the man saying a second time, "You are to me like the back of my mother." Thus expiation is not incurred by the utterance itself, but only by the second one. This is the position of the Ahl al-Zahir (the Literalists, or Zahiri school). It is also reported from Bukayr ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Ashajj, Abu al-Aliyah, and Abu Hanifa, and it is the view of al-Farra'. Tawus, Qatada, al-Zuhri, al-Hasan, Malik, and a group of scholars said: ﴿what they said﴾ means "for intercourse." The meaning is: for what they said, that they would not go back to it. So if a man makes zihar (the pre-Islamic form of divorce in which a husband compares his wife to his mother's back) and then has intercourse, expiation becomes obligatory for him, even if he divorces her or she dies. Abu Hanifa, Malik as well, al-Shafi'i, and a group said: the meaning is that they go back on what they said by resolving to retain her and to have intercourse. Whenever he resolves on that, expiation becomes obligatory for him, whether he divorces her or she dies. Al-Shafi'i said: the return that makes expiation obligatory is that he withholds from divorcing her after zihar, and a period of time passes in which he could have divorced her but does not. Some said: the meaning is: "Those who make zihar from their wives in the Jahiliyyah (the pre-Islamic period of ignorance)", that is, zihar was their custom, and then they return to that practice in Islam. This was stated by al-Qutabi. Al-Akhfash said: there is an inversion (taqdim wa ta'khir) in it, and the intended sense is: ﴿then freeing a neck﴾ for what they said. This view is worthless, because it disrupts the composition of the verse.

﴿freeing a neck﴾. The apparent meaning is that any neck (any slave) suffices, so a non-believing slave is acceptable. Malik and al-Shafi'i said: Islam is a condition for it, as with the slave in expiation for killing. The apparent meaning is that a mukatab (a slave who has contracted to purchase his freedom) is acceptable, because he is still a slave as long as a single dirham remains owed. Abu Hanifa and his companions also held this. If someone frees half of two slaves, it is not sufficient, according to Abu Hanifa and his companions. Al-Shafi'i said it is sufficient.

﴿before they touch one another﴾. It is not permitted for the one who has made zihar to have intercourse until he has made expiation. If he does so, he has sinned, and the expiation is not waived from him. Mujahid said: another expiation is incurred upon him. It was also said: the expiation obligatory upon him falls away, and nothing else is incumbent on him. The hadith of Aws ibn al-Samit refutes this view. This applies whether the expiation is by freeing a slave, by fasting, or by feeding the poor. Abu Hanifa said: if the expiation is by feeding, it is permissible for him to have intercourse and then feed the poor. This is the apparent meaning of His words: ﴿but whoever cannot, then feeding sixty needy persons﴾, since He did not say in it: ﴿before they touch one another﴾, while He did attach that condition to freeing and fasting. The apparent meaning of al-tamassu ("touching") is the literal sense, so it is not permissible for them to touch one another before it, nor to lie together, nor any other forms of enjoyment. This is the view of Malik and one of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i. Most scholars said it means intercourse, so it is permissible for him to enjoy his wife in other ways before making expiation. This was said by al-Hasan and al-Thawri, and it is the sound position in the school of al-Shafi'i. The pronoun in (yatamassa) refers to what the discourse has referred to, namely the one who made zihar and the wife to whom it was made.

﴿That is what you are admonished with﴾. The demonstrative refers to the freeing. That is, it is an act of admonition for you, so that you may refrain from zihar.

﴿But whoever does not find﴾: that is, a neck, nor its price, or he finds it or its price but needs that money. Abu Hanifa said: he is obliged to free a slave even if he needs the money, and he does not move on to fasting. This is the apparent meaning. Al-Shafi'i said: he moves on to fasting. The two months are by the crescent moons, even if one of them comes out short, or [they are counted] by number rather than by the crescent. So he fasts until the new moon, then one month by the crescent, then he completes the first by number. The apparent meaning is that consecutiveness is obligatory. If he breaks the fast without an excuse, he must start again, or if he breaks it with an excuse such as travel or the like. Ibn al-Musayyab, Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, Amr ibn Dinar, al-Sha'bi, Malik, and al-Shafi'i in one of his two opinions said: he continues building on what he has done. Al-Nakha'i, Ibn Jubayr, al-Hakam ibn Uyayna, al-Thawri, the people of ra'y (opinion), and al-Shafi'i in one of his opinions said otherwise. The apparent meaning is that if he finds a neck after he has begun fasting, he continues fasting, and it suffices for him. This is the school of Malik and al-Shafi'i. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: he is obliged to free a slave. If he has intercourse during the course of the fast, the consecutiveness is broken and he begins again. Malik and Abu Hanifa also said this. Al-Shafi'i said: it is broken if he has intercourse during the day, but not at night.

﴿But whoever is not able﴾ to fast because of a chronic illness, or because fasting weakens him severely. This is as in the hadith of Aws, when he was asked: "Are you able to fast two consecutive months?" He replied: "By God, O Messenger of God, if I do not eat for a day and a night three times, my sight fails and I fear my eyes will go blind." (ﷺ). The apparent meaning is that feeding is unrestricted, but the custom of feeding at the time of revelation specifies it, which is what satisfies people without a fixed measure of a mudd. The school of Malik holds that it is a mudd and a third by the Prophetic mudd (ﷺ). Feeding the entire number, sixty, is obligatory according to Malik and al-Shafi'i, and this is the apparent meaning. Abu Hanifa and his companions said: if one feeds one needy person half a sa' each day until he completes the number, it suffices for him.

﴿That is so that you may believe﴾. Ibn Atiyya said: the demonstrative refers to the return and to the facilitation in the act from freeing to fasting and feeding. Then He emphasized with His words: ﴿And these are the limits of God﴾: that is, hold to them and stop at them. Then He threatened the disbelievers with this legal ruling. Al-Zamakhshari said: that is the explanation, instruction, and drawing attention to the rulings, so that you may affirm belief in God and His Messenger in acting upon the laws He has prescribed concerning zihar and other matters, and abandon what you were upon in your jahiliyyah, ﴿and these are the limits of God﴾, which may not be transgressed, and ﴿for the disbelievers﴾ who do not follow them or act upon them, ﴿is a painful punishment.﴾ End of quotation.

﴿Indeed, those who oppose God and His Messenger﴾. It was revealed concerning the polytheists of Quraysh, who were humiliated on the day of the Trench by defeat, just as those who fought the messengers before them were humiliated. When He mentioned the believers who stop at His limits, He mentioned those who oppose and differ from them. Al-muhadda means enmity and opposition concerning the limits. (kubitu): Qatada said: they were humiliated. Al-Suddi said: they were cursed. It was said: this is the dialect of Madhhij. Ibn Zayd and Abu Rawq said: they were turned back in disgrace. Al-Farra' said: they were enraged on the day of the Trench.

﴿As those before them were humiliated﴾: that is, those who fought the prophets. It was also said: on the day of Badr. Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: they were destroyed. From Abu Ubayda: the ta' is a substitute for the dal, meaning kubidu: a disease struck their livers. It was said: those before them are the hypocrites of the nations. It was said: kubitu has the sense of sa-yukbatun ("they will be humiliated"), and this is good news to the believers of victory. He expressed it in the past tense to affirm that it will certainly occur. The discussion of the root kabata has already passed in Al 'Imran.

﴿And We have sent down clear signs﴾ as proof of the truthfulness of Muhammad (ﷺ) and the soundness of what he brought. (For the disbelievers): that is, those who oppose him, ﴿is a humiliating punishment﴾: that is, it will humiliate and abase them. The governing element of "the day He raises them" is either what governs "for the disbelievers" or "humiliating," or "mention," or the phrase is an answer to someone who asked: "When will be the punishment of these people?" So it was said to him: ﴿The day God raises them﴾: that is, it will be on the day God raises them. (Jami'an) is in the accusative as a state (hal): that is, gathered in one place, or its meaning is all of them, since jami' may bear both meanings. ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did﴾, as a rebuke and reproach to them. (Ahsahu) with all its details, its quantity, its manner, its time and its place. (Nasuhu): because of their belittling of it and their disdain that any reckoning would fall upon them for it. (Shahid): nothing is hidden from Him. The majority read ma yakunu with the ya'; Abu Ja'far, Abu Haywa, and Shayba read it with the ta', because al-najwa is feminine. Sahib al-Lawami said: if it is governed by the preposition, it is in the position of: "What came to me from a woman," except that in this construction the masculine is more common, in agreement with the common reading. He said: because it is attached to "from secret counsel," and that requires the collective, which is masculine. End of quotation. But the feminine is not more common in this construction, because min is extra. The verb is attributed to a feminine noun, so the feminine is more common, and it is the analogical form, as God says: ﴿And there does not come to them any sign from the signs of their Lord﴾ [al-An'am: 4], ﴿No nation precedes its term﴾ [al-Hijr: 5]. Here the verb is complete (taamma), and najwa may be a verbal noun (masdar) added to three, that is, from the secret talk of three, or a verbal noun with an omitted modifier, that is, from those who hold secret counsel, or a verbal noun applied to the group conversing secretly, so "three" is in those two readings. Ibn Atiyya said: it is a substitute or an attribute. Al-Zamakhshari said: an attribute. Ibn Abi Ablah read thalatha and khamsa in the accusative as states, with the governing element being yatanajawna implied, indicated by najwa. Al-Zamakhshari said: or by interpreting najwa as "those conversing secretly," and its accusative is from the pronoun in it. Ibn Isa said: every secret conversation is najwa. Ibn Surraqa said: sirar is what occurs between two, and najwa is what occurs among more. It was said: it was revealed concerning the hypocrites, and the three and the five were singled out because the hypocrites used to converse secretly in these two numbers to enrage the people of faith. The clause after illa in the three places is in the position of a state, and His being the fourth of them, the sixth of them, and with them through knowledge and awareness of what they converse about. Ibn Abbas said: it was revealed concerning Rabi'a and Habib, the two sons of Amr, and Safwan ibn Umayya. They talked, and one of them said: "Do you think God knows what we say?" The other said: "He knows some of it and does not know some of it." The third said: "If He knows some of it, then He knows all of it."

﴿Nor less than that﴾: this refers to the three and the five. Less than three is two, and less than five is four. ﴿Nor more﴾ indicates what follows six and beyond. The majority read (wa la akthara) in conjunction with the form of the genitive; al-Hasan, Ibn Abi Ishaq, al-A'mash, Abu Haywa, Sallam, and Ya'qub read it in the nominative, in conjunction with the position of najwa if it is meant as those conversing. Whoever makes it a pure verbal noun with an omitted modifier, meaning "nor secret conversation less," then the modifier is omitted and the modified (the pronoun) is placed in its position, and it is inflected by its inflection. It is permissible that (wa la adna) be a subject, and the predicate is ﴿except that He is with them﴾, so it is a conjunction of sentences. Al-Hasan also, Mujahid, al-Khalil ibn Ahmad, and Ya'qub also read wa la akbara with a ba' and nominative, and this admits two grammatical analyses: conjunction with the position, or nominative as a subject. It was read (yunbi'uhum) with lightening and hamza; Zayd ibn Ali read it with lightening and no hamza, with a kasra on the ha'. The majority read it with emphasis, hamza, and a damma on the ha'.

[p. 236]

*Allah's words, "Have you not seen those who were forbidden from secret counsel (najwa), then they return to what they were forbidden and hold secret counsel together in sin, enmity, and disobedience to the Messenger? And when they come to you, they greet you with a greeting with which Allah has not greeted you, and they say to themselves, 'Why does Allah not punish us for what we say?' Hell is sufficient for them; they will burn in it, and it is a wretched destination"* (58:8). *"O you who have believed, when you hold secret counsel, do not hold it together in sin, enmity, and disobedience to the Messenger, but hold it together in righteousness and piety. And fear Allah, to whom you will be gathered"* (58:9). *"Secret counsel is only from Satan, so that he may grieve those who have believed, but it harms them not at all, except by Allah's permission. And upon Allah let the believers rely"* (58:10). *"O you who have believed, when you are told, 'Make room in the assemblies,' then make room; Allah will make room for you. And when you are told, 'Rise up,' then rise up; Allah will raise those of you who have believed and those who have been given knowledge by degrees. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do"* (58:11). *"O you who have believed, when you consult the Messenger privately, then present before your private consultation a charity. That is better for you and purer. But if you do not find [anything], then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful"* (58:12). *"Are you apprehensive about presenting charities before your private consultation? So when you do not do so, and Allah has forgiven you, then establish prayer, give zakat, and obey Allah and His Messenger. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do"* (58:13).

The verse "Have you not seen" (ألم تر) was revealed concerning the Jews and the hypocrites. They would hold secret counsel apart from the believers, looking at them and winking at one another about them, deceiving the believers' relatives into thinking that some harm had befallen them, and they would continue doing this until their relatives arrived. When this became frequent among them, the believers complained to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and he ordered them not to hold secret counsel apart from the believers. They did not desist, so the verse was revealed. This is related from Ibn 'Abbas. Mujahid said: it was revealed concerning the Jews. Ibn al-Sa'ib said: concerning the hypocrites.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read *wa-yatanajawna* (ويتناجون). Hamzah, Talhah, al-A'mash, Yahya ibn Wathhab, and Ruways read *wa-yantajuna* (وينتجون), the present tense of *intaja* (انتجى).

*Bi-ma lam yuhayyika bihi Allah* (بما لم يحيك به الله): they would say, "as-sammu 'alayka" (the poison/death be upon you), and that means death. So he would reply to them, "wa-'alaykum" (and upon you). The greeting of Allah to His prophets is: *"And peace upon His servants whom He has chosen"* (27:59).

*Law la yu'adhdhibuna Allah bi-ma naqulu* (لولا يعذبنا الله بما نقول): that is, "If he were a prophet, why does he not invoke [Allah] against us so that we would be punished for what we say?" So the Exalted said: *"Hell is sufficient for them."*

Then He forbade the believers that their secret counsel should be like the secret counsel of the disbelievers. He began with sin (الإثم) because of its generality, then with enmity (العدوان) because of its gravity in souls, since it concerns the wrongs done to people. Then He ascended to what is greater, which is disobedience to the Messenger (peace be upon him), and in this there is a rebuke of the hypocrites, since their secret counsel was about this. The majority read *fa-la tatanajaw* (فلا تتناجوا), and Ibn Muhaysin assimilated the second *ta'* into the first *ta'*. The Kufans, al-A'mash, Abu Hayawah, and Ruways read *fa-la tantajaw* (فلا تنتجوا), the present form of *intaja*. The majority read the *'ayn* of *al-'udwan* with a *damma*, while Abu Hayawah read it with a *kasra* wherever it occurs. Al-Dahhak read *wa-ma'siyati al-rasul* (ومعصيات الرسول) in the plural. The majority read it in the singular. 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) read: *idha intajaytum fa-la tantajaw* (إذا انتجيتم فلا تنتجوا).

The *al-* (الـ) in *innama al-najwa* (إنما النجوى) is for specific reference, referring to the secret counsel of the disbelievers, "with sin and enmity." Its being "from Satan" is because he is the one who makes it attractive to them, so it is as if it came from him.

*Li-yahzuna alladhina amanu* (ليحزن الذين آمنوا): they would deceive the believers into thinking that their warriors had been defeated and their relatives killed. *(Wa-laysa)*: that is, the secret counsel, or Satan, or the grief, *(bi-darrihim)*: that is, the believers, *illa bi-idhni Allah*: that is, by His will, so He decrees killing or defeat.

Ibn Zayd said: it refers to the secret counsel of a group of Muslims who intended to consult the Messenger (ﷺ) privately, though they had no need or necessity, wanting only to show off by doing so. The Muslims would then suppose that it concerned news of the future, and would be heading toward it. 'Atiyyah al-'Awfi said: it was revealed concerning the private conversation that a believer sees in sleep which distresses him, so it is as if it were a private conversation with which he is addressed. End of quote. This statement does not fit with what comes before the verse or after it. The two recitations were mentioned previously regarding *li-yahzuna* (ليحزن). It is also read with a *fatha* on the *ya'* and the *zay*, in which case *alladhina* (الذين) is the subject, and in both recitations it is the object.

When Allah the Exalted forbade the believers from what causes hatred and aversion, He commanded them with what causes affection and closeness, saying: *"O you who have believed"* (the verse). Mujahid, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: they used to compete for places in the assembly of the Messenger (ﷺ), so they were commanded that some should make room for others. Ibn 'Abbas said: what is meant is the assemblies of fighting when they line up for battle. Al-Hasan and Yazid ibn Abi Habib said: the Companions would vie for the first row, not making room for one another out of desire for martyrdom, so this verse was revealed.

The majority read *tafassahu* (تفسحوا). Dawud ibn Abi Hind, Qatadah, and 'Isa read *tafasahu* (تفاسحوا). The majority read *fi al-majalis* (في المجالس) in the plural. 'Asim, Qatadah, and 'Isa read *fi al-majlis* (في المجلس) in the singular. It is also read *fi al-majlasi* (في المجلَس) with a *fatha* on the *lam*, which is the act of sitting, meaning: be spacious in your sitting and do not crowd one another in it. The apparent meaning is that the ruling applies generally to assemblies devoted to acts of obedience, even though the occasion was the assembly of the Messenger (ﷺ). It is also said that the verse is specific to the assembly of the Messenger (peace be upon him), and likewise assemblies of knowledge. This is supported by the reading of whoever reads *fi al-majalis*, and the plural is interpreted as meaning that each person has a place in the house of the Messenger (ﷺ). *Yafsahi Allah* (يفسح الله) is in the jussive mood as a response to the imperative in *fa-ifsahu*. Regarding what Allah will make room for them in, there are several views: in His mercy; or in your dwellings in Paradise; or in your graves; or in your hearts; or in this world and the Hereafter.

*Wa-idha qila insuzu* (وإذا قيل انشزوا): that is, rise up (انهضوا) from the assembly for making room, because one who wishes to make space for a newcomer rises upward, so the place becomes more spacious. They were first commanded to make room, and then secondly to comply with the command when they are ordered. Al-Hasan, Qatadah, and al-Dahhak said: its meaning is that when they are called to fight, prayer, or obedience, they should rise. It is also said: when they are called to leave the assembly of the Messenger (ﷺ), they should rise, because he (peace be upon him) at times preferred solitude in matters of Islam. Abu Ja'far, Shaybah, al-A'raj, Ibn 'Amir, Nafi', and Hafs read the *sin* (س) with a *damma* in both words. Al-Hasan, al-A'mash, Talhah, and the rest of the seven read it with a *kasra*.

The apparent meaning is that His words *"and those who have been given knowledge"* (والذين أوتوا العلم) are conjoined to *"those who have believed"* (الذين آمنوا). The conjunction indicates difference, and it is a conjunction of attributes, the meaning being: Allah will raise the believing scholars by degrees, so the two descriptions apply to one and the same entity. Ibn Mas'ud and others said: the sentence is complete at His words *"from among you"* (منكم), and *"and those who have been given knowledge"* is in the accusative by a hidden verb whose estimated meaning is: "and He will particularly grant those who have been given knowledge degrees." So for the believers there is elevation, and for the scholars there are degrees.

*Bayna yadayy najwakum* (بين يدي نجواكم): a metaphor, and the meaning is "before your secret counsel." From Ibn 'Abbas and Qatadah: some of the believers, and those who were negligent of them, frequently held private consultations with the Messenger (peace be upon him) without any need, only to show their rank. "He (ﷺ) was generous and would not turn anyone away," so this verse was revealed, imposing a strict rule concerning private consultation. It is said this ruling was abrogated before it was put into practice. Qatadah said: it was acted upon for an hour of a day. Muqatil said: for ten days. 'Ali, may Allah honor his face, said: no one acted upon it except me. I wished to consult the Messenger privately, and I had one dinar, so I exchanged it for ten dirhams, and I consulted him ten times, giving a dirham in charity each time. Then the hardship of this became evident to people, so the concession was revealed, allowing the abandonment of charity. The reading *sadaqat* (صدقات) in the plural is also transmitted. Ibn 'Abbas said: it was abrogated by the verse that follows it. It is also said: by the verse of zakat.

*A-ashfaqtum* (أأشفقتم): did you fear, that is, were you afraid of losing wealth through charity, or of being unable to find what you would give in charity? *Fa-idh lam taf'alu* (فإذ لم تفعلوا): when you did not do what you were commanded, *wa-taba Allah 'alaykum* (وتاب الله عليكم): He excused you and gave you leave not to do it. So do not neglect the prayer, zakat, and acts of obedience.

'Ayyash, from Abu 'Amr, read *bi-ma ya'malun* (بما يعملون) with a *ya'* at the beginning. The majority read it with a *ta'*.

(p-238) **﴿Those who turned to a people with whom Allah is angry, who are neither of you nor of them, and who swear falsely while they know.﴾** **﴿Allah has prepared for them a severe punishment. Indeed, evil is what they used to do.﴾** **﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and so they averted [people] from the way of Allah; for them is a humiliating punishment.﴾** **﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah. They are the companions of the Fire; they will abide therein forever.﴾** **﴿On the Day when Allah will resurrect them all, and they will swear to Him as they swear to you, and they will think that they are upon something. Unquestionably, they are the liars.﴾** **﴿Satan has overcome them and caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah. Those are the party of Satan. Unquestionably, the party of Satan are the losers.﴾** **﴿Indeed, those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, they are among the most humiliated.﴾** **﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail." Indeed, Allah is Strong and Mighty.﴾** **﴿You will not find a people who believe in Allah and the Last Day loving those who oppose Allah and His Messenger, even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kinsfolk. Those — He has written faith into their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him. And He will admit them into gardens beneath which rivers flow, abiding therein. Allah is pleased with them, and they are pleased with Him. Those are the party of Allah. Unquestionably, the party of Allah are the successful.﴾**

**﴿Those who turned﴾**: they are the hypocrites (munafiqun). **"Those with whom Allah is angry"**: they are the Jews, according to al-Suddi and Muqatil, [who said that] the Prophet (ﷺ) said to his companions: "A man will enter upon you whose heart is the heart of a tyrant and who looks with the eyes of a devil." Then 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul entered, and he was blue-eyed, dark, short, and sparse-bearded. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: "Why do you and your companions revile me?" He swore by Allah that he had not done so. The Prophet (peace be upon him) said to him: "You did." Then he brought his companions, and they swore by Allah that they had not reviled him. [Then] it was revealed.

The pronoun in **﴿ma hum﴾** refers back to **﴿those who turned﴾**, who are the hypocrites: i.e., they are not from you, O believers. **﴿Nor of them﴾**: i.e., they are not from those to whom they turned, who are the Jews. **"Ma hum"** is a resumptive statement (isti'naf) informing that they are wavering (mudhabdhabun), neither to these nor to those, as the Prophet (peace be upon him) said: "The likeness of the hypocrite is the likeness of a lone sheep wandering between two flocks: for he is with the believers in his speech, and with the disbelievers in his heart."

Ibn 'Atiyyah said: it may bear another interpretation, namely that his saying **"ma hum"** refers to the Jews, and his saying **"wa la minhum"** refers to the hypocrites. On this interpretation, the description of the hypocrites is more fitting, because they turned to people upon whom anger has fallen; they are not of their own kind, so their protection does not bind them, nor are they of the rightly-guided people, so that alliance would be proper. End of quote. The apparent interpretation, however, is the first, because **"those who turned"** are the ones being spoken about. The pronoun in **﴿wa yahlifuna﴾** ("and they swear") refers back to them, so the pronouns are consistent for them and do not differ. On this interpretation, **"ma hum"** is a resumptive statement, though it could also be a circumstantial clause (hal) from the pronoun in **"tawallaw"**. On Ibn 'Atiyyah's reading, **"ma hum"** is a qualifier of **"qawman"** (a people).

**﴿And they swear falsely﴾**: either they did not revile him, as is related regarding the occasion of revelation (sabab al-nuzul), or [the falsehood lies in] their claim to be Muslims. The falsehood is what they claimed of Islam.

**﴿While they know﴾**: a circumstantial clause (jumlah ḥaliyyah) that censures them, since they swore contrary to what they concealed. The meaning is: while they knowingly and deliberately [do so]. **"The severe punishment"**: that prepared for them in the Hereafter.

The majority read **"aymanahum"** as the plural of **yamin** (oath). Al-Hasan read **"iymanahum"** with a kasra on the hamza, meaning what they display of faith. **"Junnah"**: that by which they shield themselves and guard against what is feared, namely a shield (turs). **"Fa-sadду"**: i.e., they turned away, or they averted people from Islam, since they would discourage whomever they met from Islam and weaken the matter of faith and its adherents; or they averted the Muslims from killing them by displaying faith, while killing them is "the way of Allah" concerning them, but what they displayed of Islam averted the Muslims from killing them.

**﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾**: the discussion of this sentence has preceded at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran.

**﴿Then they will swear to Him﴾**: i.e., to Allah the Exalted. Do you not see their saying: **﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾** [al-An'am: 23]? **﴿As they swear to you﴾** that they are believers, while they are not believers. It is astonishing regarding them: how do they believe that their disbelief is hidden from the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and treat Him as if He had no knowledge of their disbelief and hypocrisy? The intended meaning is that they persist in lying, having accustomed themselves to it, so that it was on their tongues in the Hereafter just as it was in this world. **﴿And they think that they are upon something﴾**: i.e., something beneficial to them.

**﴿Satan has overcome them﴾**: i.e., he encompassed them from every direction, prevailed over their souls, and gained control over them. This root was discussed in His saying, Exalted is He: **﴿Did we not overcome you?﴾** [an-Nisa': 141] in Surat an-Nisa', and that it derives from **hāza al-himar al-ʿanah** (the donkey gathered the wild cows) when he drove them, and gathering them is usually taking possession of them; and from it comes the saying "he was a ḥawdhī, unique in his kind." 'Umar read **"istaḥāda"**, bringing it to its original form. The analogical form is **"istaḥwadha"**, which is anomalous in analogy but eloquent in usage.

**﴿So He caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah﴾**: so they do not remember Him, neither in their hearts nor with their tongues. **"The party of Satan"**: his army, as Abu 'Ubaydah said.

**﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾**: this is an elative form (ism al-tafḍil), meaning among the group of those who are the most humiliated of Allah's creatures; you will not see anyone more humiliated than them. It is related from Muqatil: when Allah opened Makkah to the believers, and al-Ta'if, Khaybar, and what was around them, they said: "We hope that Allah will make us victorious over Persia and Rome." Then 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: (p-239) "Do you think Rome and Persia are like some of the villages over which you were defeated? By Allah, they are far greater in number and more powerful in might than that you should suppose such about them." Then it was revealed: **﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾**. **"Kataba"** means: in the Preserved Tablet, or decreed. Qatadah said: it means "said." **"And My messengers"**: those among them I sent with war, and those among them I sent with proof.

**﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong﴾**: He gives victory to His party. **"Mighty"**: He protects them from being humiliated.

**﴿You will not find a people﴾**: al-Zamakhshari said, by way of imagery (takhyil): he imagined that it is impossible and inconceivable to find believing people who love the polytheists; the purpose is that this should not be, and that it should be prevented and never found in any circumstance, as an exaggeration in prohibiting it, in deterring from being involved with it, and in firmness in distancing oneself from the enemies of Allah. He increased this emphasis by His saying: **﴿even if they were their fathers﴾**. End of quote. He began with the fathers because obedience to them is obligatory upon the children, so He forbade them from loving them. He, Exalted, said: **﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, and keep them company in this world with kindness﴾** [Luqman: 15]. Then He mentioned the sons, because they are most attached to the heart. Then He mentioned the brothers third, because mutual support lies in them, as it is said:

*"Your brother, your brother; for whoever has no brother is like one who goes to battle without a weapon."*

Then fourth, the kinsfolk, because in them is mutual support, and from them come fighting, overpowering, and haste toward what they are called to, as he said:

*"They do not ask their brother when he calls them to aid in calamities, on what proof [he calls]."*

The majority read **"kataba"** in the active voice, with **"al-iman"** in the accusative, meaning Allah wrote. Abu Haywah and al-Mufaddal from 'Asim read **"kutiba"** in the passive voice, with **"al-iman"** in the nominative. The majority read **"aw 'ashiratahum"** in the singular; Abu Raja' read it in the plural. The meaning is: He established faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him, Exalted, which is guidance, light, and gentle kindness. It was said: the spirit is the Qur'an. It was said: Jibril on the day of Badr. It was said: the pronoun in **"minhu"** refers to faith, and a human being in himself is a spirit by which the believer lives. The reference in **"ula'ika"** ("those") is to those who do not love whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger. It was said: the verse was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. It was said: the apparent meaning is that it is connected to the verses about the hypocrites who were allied with the Jews. It was said: it was revealed concerning Ibn Ubayy and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: Ibn Ubayy reviled the Messenger, so Abu Bakr struck him a blow that knocked him down. The Messenger (peace be upon him) said to him: "Did you do that?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do not return to it." He said: "By Allah, if the sword were near me, I would have killed him."

It was said: it concerns Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father 'Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah on the day of Uhud; and concerning Abu Bakr, who called his son to single combat on the day of Badr; and concerning Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, who killed his brother Ibn 'Umayr on the day of Uhud. Ibn Shawdhab said: on the day of Badr. And concerning 'Umar, who killed his maternal uncle al-'As ibn Hisham on the day of Badr; and concerning 'Ali, Hamzah, and 'Ubaydah ibn al-Harith, who killed 'Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn 'Utbah on the day of Badr. Al-Waqidi said regarding the story of Abu 'Ubaydah that he killed his father. He said: "So say the people of Syria. But I asked men from the Banu Fihr, and they said: his father died before Islam." Al-Hasan read **"iymanahum"** with a kasra on the hamza, meaning what they display of faith. **"Junnah"**: that by which they shield themselves and guard against what is feared, namely a shield (turs). **"Fa-sadду"**: i.e., they turned away, or they averted people from Islam, since they would discourage whomever they met from Islam and weaken the matter of faith and its adherents; or they averted the Muslims from killing them by displaying faith, while killing them is "the way of Allah" concerning them, but what they displayed of Islam averted the Muslims from killing them.

**﴿Neither their wealth nor their children will avail them anything against Allah﴾**: the discussion of this sentence has preceded at the beginning of Surat Al 'Imran.

**﴿Then they will swear to Him﴾**: i.e., to Allah the Exalted. Do you not see their saying: **﴿By Allah, our Lord, we were not polytheists﴾** [al-An'am: 23]? **﴿As they swear to you﴾** that they are believers, while they are not believers. It is astonishing regarding them: how do they believe that their disbelief is hidden from the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and treat Him as if He had no knowledge of their disbelief and hypocrisy? The intended meaning is that they persist in lying, having accustomed themselves to it, so that it was on their tongues in the Hereafter just as it was in this world. **﴿And they think that they are upon something﴾**: i.e., something beneficial to them.

**﴿Satan has overcome them﴾**: i.e., he encompassed them from every direction, prevailed over their souls, and gained control over them. This root was discussed in His saying, Exalted is He: **﴿Did we not overcome you?﴾** [an-Nisa': 141] in Surat an-Nisa', and that it derives from **hāza al-himar al-ʿanah** (the donkey gathered the wild cows) when he drove them, and gathering them is usually taking possession of them; and from it comes the saying "he was a ḥawdhī, unique in his kind." 'Umar read **"istaḥāda"**, bringing it to its original form. The analogical form is **"istaḥwadha"**, which is anomalous in analogy but eloquent in usage.

**﴿So He caused them to forget the remembrance of Allah﴾**: so they do not remember Him, neither in their hearts nor with their tongues. **"The party of Satan"**: his army, as Abu 'Ubaydah said.

**﴿Those are among the most humiliated﴾**: this is an elative form (ism al-tafḍil), meaning among the group of those who are the most humiliated of Allah's creatures; you will not see anyone more humiliated than them. It is related from Muqatil: when Allah opened Makkah to the believers, and al-Ta'if, Khaybar, and what was around them, they said: "We hope that Allah will make us victorious over Persia and Rome." Then 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy said: (p-239) "Do you think Rome and Persia are like some of the villages over which you were defeated? By Allah, they are far greater in number and more powerful in might than that you should suppose such about them." Then it was revealed: **﴿Allah has decreed: "I and My messengers will surely prevail"﴾**. **"Kataba"** means: in the Preserved Tablet, or decreed. Qatadah said: it means "said." **"And My messengers"**: those among them I sent with war, and those among them I sent with proof.

**﴿Indeed, Allah is Strong﴾**: He gives victory to His party. **"Mighty"**: He protects them from being humiliated.

**﴿You will not find a people﴾**: al-Zamakhshari said, by way of imagery (takhyil): he imagined that it is impossible and inconceivable to find believing people who love the polytheists; the purpose is that this should not be, and that it should be prevented and never found in any circumstance, as an exaggeration in prohibiting it, in deterring from being involved with it, and in firmness in distancing oneself from the enemies of Allah. He increased this emphasis by His saying: **﴿even if they were their fathers﴾**. End of quote. He began with the fathers because obedience to them is obligatory upon the children, so He forbade them from loving them. He, Exalted, said: **﴿And if they strive with you to make you associate with Me that of which you have no knowledge, do not obey them, and keep them company in this world with kindness﴾** [Luqman: 15]. Then He mentioned the sons, because they are most attached to the heart. Then He mentioned the brothers third, because mutual support lies in them, as it is said:

*"Your brother, your brother; for whoever has no brother is like one who goes to battle without a weapon."*

Then fourth, the kinsfolk, because in them is mutual support, and from them come fighting, overpowering, and haste toward what they are called to, as he said:

*"They do not ask their brother when he calls them to aid in calamities, on what proof [he calls]."*

The majority read **"kataba"** in the active voice, with **"al-iman"** in the accusative, meaning Allah wrote. Abu Haywah and al-Mufaddal from 'Asim read **"kutiba"** in the passive voice, with **"al-iman"** in the nominative. The majority read **"aw 'ashiratahum"** in the singular; Abu Raja' read it in the plural. The meaning is: He established faith in their hearts and strengthened them with a spirit from Him, Exalted, which is guidance, light, and gentle kindness. It was said: the spirit is the Qur'an. It was said: Jibril on the day of Badr. It was said: the pronoun in **"minhu"** refers to faith, and a human being in himself is a spirit by which the believer lives. The reference in **"ula'ika"** ("those") is to those who do not love whoever opposes Allah and His Messenger. It was said: the verse was revealed concerning Hatib ibn Abi Balta'ah. It was said: the apparent meaning is that it is connected to the verses about the hypocrites who were allied with the Jews. It was said: it was revealed concerning Ibn Ubayy and Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him: Ibn Ubayy reviled the Messenger, so Abu Bakr struck him a blow that knocked him down. The Messenger (peace be upon him) said to him: "Did you do that?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Do not return to it." He said: "By Allah, if the sword were near me, I would have killed him."

It was said: it concerns Abu 'Ubaydah ibn al-Jarrah, who killed his father 'Abdullah ibn al-Jarrah on the day of Uhud; and concerning Abu Bakr, who called his son to single combat on the day of Badr; and concerning Mus'ab ibn 'Umayr, who killed his brother Ibn 'Umayr on the day of Uhud. Ibn Shawdhab said: on the day of Badr. And concerning 'Umar, who killed his maternal uncle al-'As ibn Hisham on the day of Badr; and concerning 'Ali, Hamzah, and 'Ubaydah ibn al-Harith, who killed 'Utbah and Shaybah, the two sons of Rabi'ah, and al-Walid ibn 'Utbah on the day of Badr. Al-Waqidi said regarding the story of Abu 'Ubaydah that he killed his father. He said: "So say the people of Syria. But I asked men from the Banu Fihr, and they said: his father died before Islam." End of quote, meaning in the pre-Islamic period (Jahiliyyah), before the appearance of Islam.

The exegetes have arranged the verse **﴿even if they were their fathers, their sons, their brothers, or their kinsfolk﴾** according to the stories of Abu 'Ubaydah, Abu Bakr, Mus'ab, 'Umar, 'Ali, Hamzah, and 'Ubaydah along with their relatives. And Allah knows best.
